schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE R1 (A INT, B INT);
CREATE TABLE R2 (A INT, B INT);
q1: SELECT X.B AS XB, Y.B AS YB FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y
q2: SELECT X1.XB AS XB, Y1.YB AS YB FROM (SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R1 AS X) AS X1, (SELECT Y.B AS YB FROM R2 AS Y) AS Y1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.B AS XB, Y.B AS YB FROM R1 AS X, R2 AS Y
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X1.XB AS XB, Y1.YB AS YB FROM (SELECT X.B AS XB FROM R1 AS X) AS X1, (SELECT Y.B AS YB FROM R2 AS Y) AS Y1
explanation: Both queries are semantically equivalent. They both join the tables R1 and R2 on the common attribute B and project the attribute B from each table as XB and YB, respectively. The difference in the syntax (Q1 uses a comma for the join, while Q2 uses the JOIN keyword) does not affect the outcome.
